summary: Any matrix cell may be the sole X-matrix violation, so every one of the n squared entries must be inspected in the worst case; a full coordinate scan matches that lower bound.

optimality.argument: Let C=n^2 be the number of cells. Start with a valid X-matrix. For any uninspected coordinate, changing a diagonal value to zero or an off-diagonal zero to one changes the correct result while preserving every inspected cell. Therefore a worst-case exact algorithm must inspect all C cells. Classifying and checking each coordinate once takes O(C) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Every coordinate can independently be the sole violation: zero on a diagonal or nonzero off both diagonals.
A nested scan visits each cell once and compares its zero status with the two diagonal equations.
Authored fixtures cover valid odd and even matrices, the shared center, zeros on each diagonal, off-diagonal nonzeros, and both public examples; regression exhausts all binary 3 by 3 matrices.
